about: Kermit Looking Out Window is a soft, moody photo of a Kermit the Frog plush toy pressed close to a window covered in raindrops, his felt head tilted up and away from the camera as he gazes into the gray outside. The blurred background and droplets make it feel like the last scene of a sad film. It is used for waiting and longing: the package that has not shipped, the text that never comes, the summer that feels a whole year away. The humor is the contrast between a goofy puppet frog and the deeply serious melancholy of the shot.
usage:
The top box usually starts the thought, such as "waiting for" or "me thinking about". The bottom box names what Kermit is staring out the window for, ideally something that is clearly not coming soon.

It suits slow builds, delayed deliveries, crushes who left you on read, the next season of a show, a refund, payday or the weekend. Quiet, wistful wording beats loud jokes here; the rainy-window mood is the punchline.
ideas: when games came with all the content
